items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: this particular day Charlie Madsen ... called me up. I said, 'Ooh, wow, great.'

ctx.x: Well, where does the 116th Street Dancing School come in?

That's Willy Martineau. That's Willy Martineau's band. Willy Martineau was a -- that was in 1927. In 1927, the year Lindbergh flew across the ocean. Yeah. Yeah, because I was working there when he flew across the ocean. Never will forget that. Took him 33 hours. Well, anyway, I was in this -- I remember I was home. I lived at 99th Street. I lived at 47 West 99th Street then, and this fellow, Charlie Madsen -- I'd never had a job like that, you know, a job where you go to work every night, every night, every…

So this particular day Charlie Madsen -- and he was a pretty good booking agent, because he was the guy who booked Fletcher Henderson. And he called me up. I said, 'Ooh, wow, great.' So he said, 'Well, there's a job open at the Dancing School.' You know, would I like to -- I said, 'Oh, fine, yes, of course.' So we went to work there at -- it was the Parody.
